name: Siteinspire
tagline: Hand-curated archive of ~8,000 well-designed websites, filtered by style, type and subject
description: Siteinspire is a long-running editorial gallery of finished websites, curated rather than crowd-voted, with roughly 8,000 entries in the archive. Every site is filed under four orthogonal filter axes — Styles (Typographic, Minimal, Grid Layout, Unusual Layout...), Types (Agencies & Consultancies 2,352, Design & Art Direction, Portfolio, Web & Interactive Design, E-Commerce), Subjects (Fashion, Art, Photography...) and Platforms — which you can stack to narrow a search. Popularity views (Today's Best / Week / Month / Year) surface what is currently resonating. It is aimed at web and brand designers looking for whole-page art direction, not at engineers looking for components.
pricing_detail: Free to browse. Sign-in exists for submissions, credits and weekly updates; no paid tier surfaced on the public pages.
agent_guidance: Use this only to give a human art direction for a marketing or portfolio site — the payload is screenshots, so you cannot extract markup, tokens or copy from it. Its real machine-usable asset is the filter vocabulary (style x type x subject), which is a decent controlled taxonomy to borrow when you need to describe a visual direction in words. Note that subpages sit behind a Vercel bot checkpoint: the homepage renders for a fetcher, deeper category pages return 429 or a JS challenge, so plan on citing the site rather than crawling it.
why_it_matters: It is the oldest surviving curated web-design archive with real editorial standards, so its filter taxonomy has effectively become the shared language for describing site styles. Any design catalog without it looks like it started in 2024.
notable_for: style x type x subject filter stacking
evidence: https://siteinspire.com (fetched, 200, taxonomy read from homepage), https://www.siteinspire.com/about (429), https://www.siteinspire.com/categories/styles (429 + Vercel Security Checkpoint via curl), web search for archive size

name: Lapa Ninja
tagline: 7,300+ landing pages plus a 57-element section index, free books and free UI kits
description: Lapa Ninja is a landing-page-specific inspiration gallery running since 2015, with 7,300+ curated landing pages and 15,000+ full-page screenshots. Beyond the main feed it slices the same corpus three ways: by category (SaaS, health, real estate and similar), by year, and — most usefully — by UI element, an index of 57+ landing-page section types such as gallery, menu, footer and transition. It also bundles a free-resources side: designer ebooks and free UI kits. It is aimed at anyone writing or art-directing a marketing page rather than an app.
pricing_detail: Browsing is free; a paid tier is advertised for unlimited category access, past versions, filtering and search. Exact price not verified — the site returned 403 to every fetch attempt.
agent_guidance: Reach for this over Siteinspire when the target is specifically a marketing or product landing page, because the /elements/ index is section-level (hero, menu, footer, gallery) rather than whole-site, which maps far better onto the blocks you would actually assemble. Do not try to crawl it — Cloudflare returned 403 to a plain fetch and to a full browser-UA fetch, so cite the section URL and let a human open it. Pair it with a real block library (shadcn blocks, Tailwind UI) for the code; Lapa only supplies the reference image.
why_it_matters: It is the only large gallery that indexes landing pages by section type rather than by whole page, which is the granularity a page actually gets built at.
evidence: https://lapa.ninja (403), https://www.lapa.ninja/ (403 via WebFetch and via curl with browser UA), https://www.lapa.ninja/categories/ (403); counts and taxonomy taken from search-result titles and snippets for lapa.ninja/, /post/, /elements/, /category/ — page body never read

name: Dribbble
tagline: The shot feed: cropped UI and branding visuals, browsable but unreadable and unlicensed
description: Dribbble is the original designer shot-sharing community: small, cropped, portfolio-grade visuals of UI, branding, illustration and motion, ranked by likes. Browsing is public and filters exist by category (Product Design, Web Design, Animation, Branding, Illustration, Mobile, Typography, Print), by 90+ colour swatches and by timeframe. Saving, contacting and hiring require an account, and PRO / PRO+ memberships gate the professional features. The v2 API is deliberately narrow — it authenticates a designer to list their own shots and does not expose public search — so there is no legitimate programmatic path into the corpus.
pricing_detail: Free to browse; account required to save or contact. PRO and PRO+ memberships exist for designers; exact member prices not shown on the public shot feed.
agent_guidance: Be blunt with the user: an agent cannot use Dribbble. A plain HTTP fetch returns 202 with an empty body, the content is a rendered image feed with no extractable structure, every shot is a designer's copyrighted work with no reuse licence, and the v2 API only returns your own shots. Send a human here for visual taste on branding and illustration, then reach for Page Flows or Mobbin when the need is an actual product flow, and for a component registry when the need is code.
why_it_matters: It defined what a design portfolio shot looks like, and its aesthetic-over-usability bias is exactly why 'dribbbleisation' became a critique — worth knowing, not worth building from.
notable_for: no reuse licence on any image
v2 API returns only your own shots
evidence: https://dribbble.com (curl: 202, 0 bytes), https://dribbble.com/shots (rendered via WebFetch, taxonomy and login behaviour read), developer.dribbble.com v2 docs via search

name: Behance
tagline: Adobe's portfolio platform: long-form creative case studies, no public API since shutdown
description: Behance is Adobe's creative portfolio network, where designers publish multi-image project case studies rather than single shots. Projects are filed by creative field — Graphic Design, Photography, Illustration, 3D Art, UI/UX, Motion, Architecture, Product Design, Fashion, Advertising, Fine Arts, Crafts, Game Design, Sound — with a second axis of Adobe tool tags (Photoshop, Illustrator, After Effects, Substance 3D). Browsing projects is public and does not require sign-in; uploading, saving and following do. Behance Pro adds analytics and a custom portfolio site on a 7-day trial. The public API was shut down, so there is no supported way to pull a user's projects programmatically.
pricing_detail: Free to browse and to publish. Behance Pro (analytics, custom portfolio domain) sold via Adobe with a 7-day free trial; exact price not shown on the homepage.
agent_guidance: Treat this as a human-only destination: the projects are image stacks inside a JS app, the public API is gone, and every project is the author's copyrighted work with no reuse grant — so never scrape it and never present a Behance image as an asset the user can ship. It beats Dribbble when someone needs the full arc of a project (research, process, final artwork) rather than a hero crop, and it is the right place to point someone hunting for a studio or a freelancer. For anything you need to read, cite the project URL and stop there.
why_it_matters: It is the largest public record of long-form creative process, which makes it the reference for how a case study is structured — even though none of it is machine-accessible.
evidence: https://behance.net -> https://www.behance.net/ (curl 200, 873KB; WebFetch read ownership, taxonomy, login behaviour, Behance Pro), search confirming the public API shutdown

name: Savee
tagline: Ad-free visual bookmarking for designers, with extensions, a Figma plugin and boards
description: Savee (savee.it now redirects to savee.com) is a visual bookmarking and moodboarding tool for designers — 'Made for visual minds' — where you save images, colours, layouts and links from anywhere on the web into boards. It positions itself against Pinterest by being ad-free and algorithm-free, with over a million users, and it ships the full capture surface: Chrome, Safari, Firefox and Edge extensions, iPhone and Android apps, and a Figma plugin. An account is needed to browse and save. Paid tiers unlock unlimited and private boards, collaboration and, on the top tier, a portfolio site with a custom domain and API access.
pricing_detail: Pro $9/user/month billed yearly. Pro & Portfolio $15/month billed yearly (portfolio site, custom domain, API access). Teams $12/user/month billed yearly, 2 users included. A free tier exists but its limits are not stated on the pricing page.
agent_guidance: Recommend this as the human's collection layer, not as a source you read — the feed is images behind a sign-in wall and none of it carries a reuse licence. It is the right answer when someone asks for 'Pinterest but for designers and without the ads', and the Figma plugin is the reason a design team picks it over a folder of screenshots. The advertised API sits only on the $15/month Pro & Portfolio tier and is aimed at the portfolio site, so do not plan an integration around it without checking first.
why_it_matters: It is where a large slice of the graphic-design and art-direction world now keeps its references, so a link to a Savee board is increasingly the format a client brief arrives in.
notable_for: browser extensions plus iOS, Android and Figma plugin
evidence: https://savee.it -> https://savee.com/ (curl 200, 198KB), https://savee.com/ (WebFetch: positioning, content types, apps and plugins), https://savee.com/pricing (WebFetch: exact tier prices)
